data.reasoning: The disagreement stems from a tool error (HTTP 400) in the qwen3-235b report during PKGBUILD review, not a genuine security disagreement. The deepseek-v4-flash report successfully reviewed both PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO, finding standard AUR packaging: upstream source from the project's own GitHub repository with pinned SHA-256 checksum, normal build/install functions using make and DESTDIR, no suspicious network operations or obfuscated commands. The package follows standard multi-package Lua binding patterns with no injection indicators.
data.disagreement_analysis: The qwen3-235b model encountered an API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) when attempting to review the PKGBUILD file, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. This is a tool failure, not a security finding. The deepseek-v4-flash model successfully completed the review and found no issues.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b report failed to complete PKGBUILD review due to LLM API error (HTTP 400)
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should be clearly distinguished from security findings in the final verdict - a failed review should not override a successful safe review when the successful review covers all critical files
When one model encounters a tool error and another completes successfully, the successful review should be weighted as the primary evidence rather than triggering an inconclusive verdict
Standard AUR patterns (GitHub sources with pinned checksums, make/make install in package functions) should be recognized as safe without requiring extensive justification
